visuals.title: Where diabetes does damage
visuals.text: Microvascular: eyes, kidneys, nerves. Macrovascular: heart and arteries. Also gastroparesis and foot ulcers.

visual.title: HbA1c
visual.caption: 42-47 is prediabetes; 48 or more is diabetes (repeat if asymptomatic).

events.x: Urine ACR, retinal screening, foot check

visuals.title: Type 2 drug pathway
nodes: Add DPP-4 inhibitor (or SU, pioglitazone, GLP-1 RA)

visuals.title: Type 1 mechanism
nodes: T cells attack islet beta cells

visuals.title: How SGLT-2 inhibitors work
nodes: Lower glucose + renal and heart protection

glossary.Metabolic disorder: A disease that disrupts the body's normal chemical processes, here handling of glucose.
glossary.Insulin deficiency: Too little insulin, from beta-cell loss (absolute) or failure to keep up with demand (relative).
glossary.Absolute insulin deficiency: Almost no insulin is made, as in Type 1 diabetes.
glossary.Relative insulin deficiency: Some insulin is made but not enough to overcome resistance, as in Type 2.
glossary.Autoimmune: When the immune system attacks the body's own tissues.
glossary.Ketosis: Raised ketones in the body from fat breakdown when insulin is lacking.
glossary.Hyperthyroidism: An overactive thyroid gland producing too much thyroid hormone.
glossary.TFTs: Thyroid function tests: TSH and free T4.
glossary.Retinopathy: Damage to the retina's blood vessels.
glossary.Polyneuropathy: Damage to many peripheral nerves, usually symmetrical and starting in the feet.
glossary.Length-dependent: Affecting the longest nerves first, so symptoms start in the toes and feet.
glossary.Matrix metalloproteinases: Enzymes that break down connective tissue; their disruption by AGEs contributes to nerve damage.
glossary.Ulceration: Formation of an open sore that breaks through the skin.
glossary.Limb ischaemia: Inadequate blood supply to a limb, threatening tissue survival.
glossary.Pseudomonas aeruginosa: A Gram-negative bacterium commonly found in diabetic foot ulcers.
glossary.Vagal tone: The background activity of the vagus nerve, which drives gut movement.
glossary.Acetylcholine: The neurotransmitter the vagus nerve uses to stimulate gut muscle.
glossary.Motility: Movement of food through the gut by muscle contraction.
glossary.Sickle cell trait: Carrying one sickle gene; it makes HbA1c less reliable.
glossary.Fasting plasma glucose: Blood glucose measured after at least 8 hours without food.
glossary.Random plasma glucose: Blood glucose measured at any time regardless of meals.
glossary.U&Es: Urea and electrolytes: a kidney function blood test.
glossary.Lipids: Blood fats such as cholesterol and triglycerides.
glossary.Anti-GAD antibodies: Antibodies against glutamic acid decarboxylase in beta cells, suggesting Type 1.
glossary.Pancreatic cancer: Cancer of the pancreas, which can present as new diabetes with weight loss in older people.
glossary.Basal: Background long-acting insulin covering needs between meals and overnight.
glossary.Bolus: A dose of rapid-acting insulin given with a meal.
glossary.BMI: Body mass index: weight in kg divided by height in metres squared.
glossary.Modified-release: A tablet that releases its drug slowly, reducing side effects such as gut upset with metformin.
glossary.Comorbidities: Other medical conditions a patient has at the same time.
glossary.Triple therapy: Treatment with three drugs at once.
glossary.ACE inhibitor: A blood pressure drug such as ramipril that blocks angiotensin production and protects the kidneys.
glossary.Pregabalin: An anti-epileptic drug used for neuropathic pain.
glossary.Duloxetine: An SNRI antidepressant used for neuropathic pain.
glossary.Gabapentin: An anti-epileptic drug used for neuropathic pain.
glossary.Tricyclic antidepressant: An older class of antidepressant, such as amitriptyline, used at low dose for nerve pain.
glossary.Insulin pump: A device that delivers insulin continuously under the skin.
glossary.Intercurrent illness: Another illness occurring during an existing condition, such as gastroenteritis.
glossary.Subcutaneously: Injected into the fat layer under the skin.
glossary.Postural hypotension: A fall in blood pressure on standing, causing dizziness; can result from autonomic neuropathy.
glossary.Islet: Clusters of hormone-making cells in the pancreas, including the insulin-making beta cells.
glossary.Glycation: Glucose sticking to proteins without an enzyme, as in HbA1c and AGEs.
glossary.Endothelium: The inner lining of blood vessels.
glossary.Basement membrane: A thin supporting layer under endothelium, thickened by diabetes in kidney and retina.
glossary.Atherosclerosis: Build-up of fatty plaques in artery walls.
glossary.Lipolysis: Breakdown of stored fat into fatty acids.
glossary.Ketogenesis: Making ketones from fatty acids in the liver.
glossary.Osmotic diuresis: Passing large volumes of urine because glucose in the tubule draws water with it.
glossary.Proximal renal tubule: The first part of the kidney tubule, where most glucose is reabsorbed.
glossary.Reabsorption: Taking substances back from the urine into the blood.
glossary.Glycaemic control: How well blood glucose is kept in the target range.
